relationships.subject: Nitric oxide
relationships.evidence_quote: There is evidence that NO can directly increase CGRP release via the TRPV1 receptor [81]

relationships.subject: nNOS
relationships.evidence_quote: nNOS promotes CGRP release from trigeminal fibres, and CGRP activates NO production via endothelial NOS (eNOS) [84].

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: nNOS promotes CGRP release from trigeminal fibres, and CGRP activates NO production via endothelial NOS (eNOS) [84].

relationships.subject: Nitroglycerin
relationships.evidence_quote: Infusion of NTG into the TNC or onto the pial surface promotes the release of CGRP, substance P, and neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) and subsequent vasodilatation [71,72]

key_findings: Review: NO and CGRP interact bidirectionally in migraine; NTG provokes migraine-like attacks and neuropeptide release.
CGRP-targeted therapies are in clinical practice; PACAP-targeted therapies are promising.
